observation: Three original recordings repeat the encounter route and retain 124 exact control artifacts each. The complete later policy interval matches all 25 actor decisions and 19 full sprite restorations, six ordinary 13 command iterations and 18 frame-list steps. A second recording independently matches six complete timer calls and four compact metadata calls/32 command positions; all 137 shared records agree. Original return-time loading reproduces both complete party resources, 163,483 bytes, including the actual adjacent-input suffixes.
interpretation: Later checkpoint restoration is a distinct stage after actor/sprite recreation. The recovered policy and checkpoint helper compose source-calculated animation, timer and frame behavior; original after-state is an oracle, never a substitute for required command effects. Only timed 13 executes in this stage. Other supported timed families, B3 and E1 have source and synthetic coverage. The four compact calls only skip ordinary parts; their auxiliary-write paths remain source/synthetic. Creation, ownership, remaining VM and readiness remain open.

validation.tolerance: Exact bytes, integers, source hashes and call boundaries. No output masks, invented decoder suffix, original-state effect substitution or native timing assumption.

original_replay.scope: Complete 25 actor checkpoint decisions and 19 sprite replay calls from qualified original entry state. Earlier transition VM records and any calls crossing the trace start are explicitly excluded. Sprite creation/rebinding and broad ordinary VM coverage remain open.

semantic_review.generic_effect_subset: 8001fbe4 B3 index-store case plus dispatch/common return only
notes: Policy updates the saved signed animation before deciding to skip. Saved full words compare to current unsigned bytes; actor layer and party-mode gates preserve order. Current actor extension flags determine the 0x174 base stride plus 12/16 bytes.

Restoration temporarily sets the rate to zero, writes renderer components with pointer reloads, selects using the post-renderer signed animation byte, then advances ordinary timers until the saved six-bit counter. Each iteration integrates old X/Z/Y velocities before vertical acceleration, then the final checkpoint restores XYZ and sequencer words.
Timer zero does not dispatch, signed rate -1 skips, and all other rates compare with the reloaded global after each iteration. Halfword decrement wrap and expiry on the original value one agree.

Ordinary frame commands use source frame lookup/list effects, signed wrapped scale products and add-before-SRA truncation, unlike facing-only replay's duration arithmetic. The six-bit step counter saturates at 63. High timed commands require incoming S3, B3 masks the source index and uses the source width, and E1 is a signed displacement relative to current PC.

Compact and standard metadata differ in their initial part-table stride and prefix. Their later command stream advances 3/5 bytes for ordinary parts and preserves the high-bit skip/auxiliary formats. Allocation remains an explicit error.

Return-time party decoder outputs, including five adjacent RAM tail bytes, qualify supplied source resources; the later menu's final RAM is not used as the source oracle. Captured complete live hashes bind each resource to the post-return RAM anchor, and actual reads additionally match decoded disc-derived bytes.

Main replay matches all nested full sprite payloads, rate/head state, stable globals, exact operation order and saved SP/RA context. Supplemental shared records have identical registers, timing and payloads and provide complete timer/compact call boundaries.

limitations: One Disc 1 field 23 ordinary encounter-victory-return route, repeated by three recordings. Main/detail exclude 423/124 earlier battle/transition records, including calls crossing the trace start. Those commands remain unreconstructed here.

Only six timed 13 commands execute during checkpoint replay. Other timed families, incoming-S3 behavior, rates, B3 and E1 have original-source/synthetic evidence only. Other high commands and alternate platform execution fail explicitly.
All four compact metadata calls consist of ordinary part skips; auxiliary writes are source/synthetic, and missing auxiliary allocation fails. No arbitrary pointer-alias or uncaptured write coverage.

Field policy source checks descriptor/transform/cursor ordering; the reusable policy function consumes one current recreated actor and checkpoint. It does not construct original actor allocations or a native field.

Party-resource identity is lifetime-specific. Actual adjacent input accounts for all ending-byte differences; later menu RAM reuse cannot replace the qualified post-return anchor. The 68 earlier field-resource changes remain outside the exact used-read claim.

Optional actor extensions, changed party modes and full return variants lack new original occurrences. Semantic state ownership, sprite creation/rebinding, rollback, native readiness, hardware cadence, full battle/menu/persistence/media and all Phase 1 slice proof domains remain open.
The generic-effect body was repaired through its original common epilogue and byte qualified. That body and other exported dependencies are not fully semantically reconstructed by this finding.
